name: Log-Gabor Filter Analysis
description: Applies log-Gabor filters for improved frequency selectivity over standard Gabor — captures AI generation signatures (Field, 1987).
mechanism:
This method applies Log-Gabor filters following Field's (1987) framework for analyzing image frequency structure:

1. **Log-Gabor Bank Construction**: A bank of Log-Gabor filters is constructed in the frequency domain with logarithmic spacing. Unlike standard Gabor filters, Log-Gabor filters have zero DC component, no bandwidth limitation, and their transfer function is Gaussian on a logarithmic frequency scale: G(f) = exp(−(log(f/f₀))²/(2(log(σ/f₀))²)).

2. **Multi-Orientation Filtering**: The filter bank spans multiple orientations (typically 6-8) and scales (4-6 octaves), providing comprehensive coverage of the 2D frequency plane. Each filter isolates a specific frequency band and orientation.

3. **Response Energy Mapping**: The local energy response is computed as E(x,y) = √(even²(x,y) + odd²(x,y)), where even and odd components are the real and imaginary parts of the filter response. This captures local frequency content independent of phase.

4. **Natural Image Statistics Comparison**: Response statistics are compared to the known 1/f amplitude spectrum of natural images. AI-generated images exhibit characteristic deviations — GANs often show spectral peaks at grid frequencies, while diffusion models may underrepresent certain frequency bands.

5. **Anomaly Scoring**: The deviation from expected natural image frequency statistics across all filter responses is aggregated into a forensic score indicating the likelihood of AI generation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
